tier_reason: Public standalone benchmark code (src/absl_lcp_lcs/bench.cc, src/absl_memcasecmp/bench.cc, src/absl_remove_ws/bench.cc on the bench/bench.h harness, driven by run_all.sh) times verbatim Abseil code (original.h) against the patch; compiler (Apple clang 14), flags (-std=c++17 -O3) and CPU (Apple M2) are stated, and raw outputs are checked in under results/.

corrections.claimed_speedup: FindLongestCommonSuffix 6.87x headline (the half_match/256 row of results/absl_lcp_lcs_bench.txt: 55.84 to 8.13 ns); FINDINGS.md table: full match 4096 B 1524 to 233 ns (6.5x), 256 B 100 to 15 ns (6.9x), half match 4096 B 754 to 121 ns (6.2x); regresses to about 0.5x (0.55 to about 1.05 ns) when the last bytes differ. memcasecmp 5.98x headline (FINDINGS.md: eq_case 256 B 229 to 38 ns; 4096 B eq_exact 1227 to 246 ns 4.99x, eq_case 3557 to 612 ns 5.82x; the checked-in results file is a slightly different run: eq_case/256 6.29x, eq_case/4096 5.97x, eq_exact/4096 4.96x); 4.1-4.3x at 16 B; mismatch at byte 0 is 0.47x (0.90 to 1.91 ns). RemoveExtraAsciiWhitespace 1.40x on already-clean 4096 B input (2460 to 1758 ns; results file 1.38x), 1.27-1.46x on clean input across sizes, but 0.78-0.84x on input with one internal double space (64-4096 B).
corrections.caveats: Baseline is Abseil's scalar loop copied verbatim into original.h (abseil-cpp@7e706921) and compiled in the same file as the patch, not glibc strncasecmp or memcmp, so the ratios say nothing about libc; one machine (Apple M2) and one compiler (Apple clang 14; 'macOS 24.5' is probably the Darwin version, i.e. macOS 15.5). Each benchmark re-runs one fixed input pair in a hot loop (cache-resident, perfectly predicted), and the eq_case workload flips every letter, the worst case for the original's per-byte branch. Raw outputs in results/ (absl_lcp_lcs_bench.txt, absl_memcasecmp_bench.txt, absl_remove_ws_bench.txt) come from a slightly different run than the FINDINGS.md tables (within a few percent). The patches regress on early mismatches (about 2x slower at 1-2 ns absolute) and RemoveExtraAsciiWhitespace is 16-28% slower when a rewrite is needed. The patches are not upstreamed to Abseil (no PR linked); the author notes FindLongestCommonSuffix has no call sites in the codebases checked. The repo's dollar and CO2 fleet estimates are heuristics, not evidence. Two more patches in the repo (nlohmann/json dump_escaped 4.62x, cpp-httplib header hash 1.44x) belong to JSON and HTTP categories and are not recorded here. Optimized code lives alongside verbatim Apache-2.0 Abseil source (original.h); the author's additions are MIT.

notes: Numbers check out against FINDINGS.md and the checked-in results files; code is correct on inspection (SWAR tolower masks to 7 bits, clz/ctz guarded against zero). Shortcomings to record: Abseil scalar loops as baseline (not libc), single Apple M2 machine, fixed hot-cache inputs, regressions on early-mismatch and needs-rewrite inputs, patches not upstreamed, 0-star repo from 2026-08.

tier_reason: First-party README prose (2012) compares against the generic libc memcpy/memset with peak MB/s figures and parity points, but gives no result tables, CPU model, compiler, flags or libc version, and the modified ssvb-membench harness is not in the repo.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 72 stars, 9 forks; packaged as libcofi (libcofi_rpi.so) in Buildroot (package/libcofi, e.g. 2017.08) and Exherbo (sys-rpi/copies-and-fills), and shipped by Arch Linux ARM until arm-mem replaced it (search snippets only)
corrections.caveats: First-party claim in a 2012 README with no CPU model, compiler, flags, libc version or result tables; the benchmark harness is a modified copy of ssvb-membench that is not in this repo. The README says the library only reaches parity with libc at 100-150 bytes, so small copies gain nothing. The ~7x memset figure is a peak MB/s compared to libc, not a general average. Hardware is unnamed; in July 2012 the only shipping board was the Raspberry Pi Model B (BCM2835, ARM1176JZF-S), so the code is ARMv6-specific (inference). Licence is stated as LGPL version 2.1 without 'or later' in the README and asm headers; there is no LICENSE file. Last commit 2012-08-03; Raspbian and Arch Linux ARM later moved to Ben Avison's arm-mem (libarmmem.so), and a commenter reported no gain on Raspberry Pi 3B/3B+ (search snippets only). The Makefile still names the pre-rename lowercase .s files.

notes: README numbers match the record (parity at ~150 B memcpy and ~100 B memset, 2-3x memcpy, 680 MB/s, 1390 MB/s memset ~7x). Shortcomings to record: first-party prose only, no hardware/compiler/libc details, harness not public, ARMv6-only and superseded by arm-mem, abandoned since 2012. Lead: bavison/arm-mem (successor used by Raspbian as libarmmem.so) is not in the catalog.

tier_reason: First-party Google Benchmark tables in the PR thread against the C runtime strlen/memchr (CSTD rows) on a stated i9-10980XE; the memchr harness (ImMemchrBench/ImMemchrGoogleBench.cpp) is public and its Visual Studio project gives MSVC v143 Release flags, but the ImStrlen benchmark code is not public, no compiler version is stated with the results, and the posted table is a subset, so not A.

corrections.baseline: C runtime strlen and memchr (labelled CSTD; ImMemchrCSTD is a plain memchr call). The bench repo is a Visual Studio 2022 project (v143 toolset, Release|x64, static CRT /MT), so CSTD is the MSVC CRT implementation, not glibc
corrections.compiler_and_flags: MSVC, Visual Studio 2022 v143 toolset (exact version not stated); ImMemchrBench.vcxproj Release|x64: /Oi, /GL whole-program optimization, /Ob2, /arch:AVX2, /MT, /std:c++latest (no Optimization element, so the MSBuild Release default /O2 applies); the README says only 'Compiled benchmark in release'
corrections.claimed_speedup: 1 GB buffer: ImStrlen AVX2_PREFETCH 56.6 ms (17.6 Gi/s) vs CSTD 79.9 ms (12.5 Gi/s), 1.41x; ImMemchr AVX2_PREFETCH 58.2 ms (17.17 Gi/s) vs CSTD 89.9 ms (10.93 Gi/s), 1.54x, which is the '55%' in the PR title; plain AVX2 ImMemchr without prefetch 79.8 ms, only 1.13x; 16 MB ImMemchr 0.799 vs 1.17 ms (1.46x); 1 MB ImStrlen 0.010 vs 0.059 ms (about 5.9x, 93.3 vs 16.4 Gi/s) (ratios derived from page data). A later comment says AVX2 ImMemchr gave 'about 60%' more performance on a 16 MB buffer and ImGui::TextUnformatted dropped from 1.6 ms to 0.98 ms per frame
corrections.caveats: Numbers are from a PR thread (ocornut/imgui #8421, still open, not merged); the bench repo README has no results table, no compiler or flags, and no LICENSE file (so reference only; the PR code would carry ImGui's licence if merged). The bench repo only benchmarks memchr: the ImStrlen code was added to the PR on 2025-03-01, after the repo's last commit, so the strlen numbers have no public harness. The posted table omits the AVX-512, UNROLL and SSE4.2 variants the harness also runs, run_benchmark.ps1 named in the README is not in the repo, and TestData::set_lines wrote past the end of the test buffer until a fix on 2025-02-23 (harness only; newline pattern unchanged). Buffers of 1 MB to 1 GB are far from typical ImGui string lengths and the 1 GB gain comes mostly from software prefetch (AVX2 without prefetch is 1.13x); the 60% figure is for one text-rendering workload. Baseline is the MSVC CRT on Windows, so gains over glibc's AVX2 strlen/memchr may be smaller. Google Benchmark's header reports 36 x 3000 MHz although the PR states a 4600 MHz all-core overclock. The maintainer only added ImStrlen/ImMemchr #define hooks to master (commit 1ec99f4, 2025-03-07) so such variants can be supplied externally, and a commenter argued these belong in the C library.

notes: PR tables match the record; the 55% title equals the 1 GB ImMemchr AVX2_PREFETCH vs CSTD ratio (derived). The memchr half nearly meets A (public harness, vcxproj flags, stated CPU) but strlen has no public code, so C overall. Shortcomings to record: PR not merged, no licence (reference), MSVC CRT baseline only, memory-bound 1 MB-1 GB buffers, gain at 1 GB mostly from prefetch, strlen harness not public, curated subset of results.
